statement: the function returns a result r and r equals the maximum, over all choices of indices 0 <= i <= j <= len(s) and 0 <= k <= l <= len(t) such that the byte sequence s[i..j) concatenated with t[k..l) is a palindrome, of (j - i) + (l - k). Empty substrings (i = j or k = l) are allowed; a sequence is a palindrome if it equals its reverse; the maximum is taken over a nonempty finite set.
preconditions: s and t are byte slices (Slice Std.U8) with 1 <= len(s) <= 30, 1 <= len(t) <= 30, and every byte of s and t is an ASCII lowercase English letter (97 <= byte <= 122).

statement: the function returns a result r (it does not fail, panic, or report overflow) for every pair s,t satisfying the preconditions.
preconditions: s and t are byte slices (Slice Std.U8) with 1 <= len(s) <= 30, 1 <= len(t) <= 30, and every byte of s and t is an ASCII lowercase English letter (97 <= byte <= 122).

statement: whenever the function returns a result r, r <= len(s) + len(t).
preconditions: s and t are byte slices (Slice Std.U8) with 1 <= len(s) <= 30, 1 <= len(t) <= 30, and every byte of s and t is an ASCII lowercase English letter (97 <= byte <= 122).

statement: whenever the function returns a result r, there exist indices 0 <= i <= j <= len(s) and 0 <= k <= l <= len(t) such that (j - i) + (l - k) = r and the concatenation s[i..j) followed by t[k..l) is a palindrome.
preconditions: s and t are byte slices (Slice Std.U8) with 1 <= len(s) <= 30, 1 <= len(t) <= 30, and every byte of s and t is an ASCII lowercase English letter (97 <= byte <= 122).

statement: whenever the function returns a result r, for every choice of indices 0 <= i <= j <= len(s) and 0 <= k <= l <= len(t), if s[i..j) followed by t[k..l) is a palindrome, then (j - i) + (l - k) <= r.
preconditions: s and t are byte slices (Slice Std.U8) with 1 <= len(s) <= 30, 1 <= len(t) <= 30, and every byte of s and t is an ASCII lowercase English letter (97 <= byte <= 122).

statement: let L(x) be the maximum length of a contiguous substring of x that is a palindrome. Whenever the function returns a result r, r >= L(s).
preconditions: s and t are byte slices (Slice Std.U8) with 1 <= len(s) <= 30, 1 <= len(t) <= 30, and every byte of s and t is an ASCII lowercase English letter (97 <= byte <= 122).

statement: let L(x) be the maximum length of a contiguous substring of x that is a palindrome. Whenever the function returns a result r, r >= L(t).
preconditions: s and t are byte slices (Slice Std.U8) with 1 <= len(s) <= 30, 1 <= len(t) <= 30, and every byte of s and t is an ASCII lowercase English letter (97 <= byte <= 122).

statement: whenever the function returns a result r, for every nonempty contiguous substring x of s, if the reverse of x occurs as a contiguous substring of t, then r >= 2 * len(x).
preconditions: s and t are byte slices (Slice Std.U8) with 1 <= len(s) <= 30, 1 <= len(t) <= 30, and every byte of s and t is an ASCII lowercase English letter (97 <= byte <= 122).

statement: if no byte value occurs in both s and t (that is, for every i,k with 0 <= i < len(s) and 0 <= k < len(t), s[i] != t[k]), then whenever the function returns a result r, r = max(L(s), L(t)), where L(x) is the maximum length of a contiguous palindromic substring of x.
preconditions: s and t are byte slices (Slice Std.U8) with 1 <= len(s) <= 30, 1 <= len(t) <= 30, and every byte of s and t is an ASCII lowercase English letter (97 <= byte <= 122).

statement: if the concatenation of all of s followed by all of t is a palindrome, then whenever the function returns a result r, r = len(s) + len(t).
preconditions: s and t are byte slices (Slice Std.U8) with 1 <= len(s) <= 30, 1 <= len(t) <= 30, and every byte of s and t is an ASCII lowercase English letter (97 <= byte <= 122).

statement: whenever the function returns a result r, if r = len(s) + len(t), then the concatenation of all of s followed by all of t is a palindrome.
preconditions: s and t are byte slices (Slice Std.U8) with 1 <= len(s) <= 30, 1 <= len(t) <= 30, and every byte of s and t is an ASCII lowercase English letter (97 <= byte <= 122).

statement: let reverse(x) be the byte sequence x read in reverse order. Whenever the function returns r on (s,t) and returns r' on (reverse(t), reverse(s)), we have r = r'.
preconditions: s and t are byte slices (Slice Std.U8) with 1 <= len(s) <= 30, 1 <= len(t) <= 30, and every byte of s and t is an ASCII lowercase English letter (97 <= byte <= 122).

statement: whenever the function returns a result r: r >= 2 if and only if at least one of the following holds: (a) there is an index i with 0 <= i and i+1 < len(s) and s[i] = s[i+1]; (b) there is an index i with 0 <= i and i+2 < len(s) and s[i] = s[i+2]; (c) there is an index i with 0 <= i and i+1 < len(t) and t[i] = t[i+1], or there is an index i with 0 <= i and i+2 < len(t) and t[i] = t[i+2]; (d) there are indices i,k with 0 <= i < len(s), 0 <= k < len(t), and s[i] = t[k].
preconditions: s and t are byte slices (Slice Std.U8) with 1 <= len(s) <= 30, 1 <= len(t) <= 30, and every byte of s and t is an ASCII lowercase English letter (97 <= byte <= 122).
